Collaborate with business and technical stakeholders including Grid Operations, IT Infrastructure, Cybersecurity, and the Business Integrator on integration deliverables. Provide support and mentorship to the engineering team on integration patterns, DERMS domain knowledge, and operational technology (OT) best practices. Contribute to IT standards, procedures, and processes for utility-grade platform integration. Ability to collaborate with cross functional teams including vendor engineering, infrastructure, cybersecurity, and testing engineers. Strong experience with infrastructure automation and VM provisioning pipelines: Terraform for Azure resource deployment; Ansible, PowerShell DSC, or similar for on-premises VM configuration and application deployment. Demonstrated ability to build fully automated, idempotent deployment pipelines that provision, configure, and validate multi-tier application environments from code with zero manual intervention. Strong knowledge of the agile software development process including PI Planning ceremonies. Solid communication and documentation skills. Position Overview The Database Administrator is responsible for the reliability, performance and security of Accanto Health's Azure data platform, which integrates data from the electronic health record, Salesforce and financial systems to support enterprise reporting and analytics. As the organization's first dedicated database administrator, this position establishes and maintains platform standards, monitoring, backup and recovery, access controls and documentation. The role administers Azure SQL and data warehouse environments, ensures the reliability of data ingestion from source systems, tunes database and reporting performance, and safeguards protected health information in accordance with HIPAA. This position partners with the Data Architect, Data Developers, and the EHR and application teams, and reports to the Director of Health Data Analytics. Schedule 8am-5pm, Monday to Friday Salary Range $150,414- $184,970 commensurate with experience Location: Remote- Must be US based, and able to work with no restrictions in the US in a remote home office. Travel up to 10% Visa / work permit sponsorship is not available for this position How Database Administrators Empower Recovery Platform and environments Azure SQL and warehouse environments across development, test and production — compute and storage sizing, performance tiers, and platform cost. Environment lifecycle, including scheduled refreshes of non-production from production so that test data is current enough to surface real edge cases. This is currently unowned and refreshes have lapsed; you will own the cadence, the vendor request process, and the cost conversation that goes with it. Ingestion reliability from the EHR, Salesforce and financial systems — monitoring, alerting, failure triage, and documented re-run procedures. Performance Tune ETL/ELT transformations and reporting queries (SSRS, Power BI). Own indexing, statistics and partitioning strategy for large tables such as claims, transactions and encounters. Establish performance baselines, so that “the report is slow” becomes a measurement rather than an argument. Security and compliance Role-based access control, least-privilege design, and periodic access review. PHI safeguards under HIPAA: encryption in transit and at rest, data masking, audit logging. Vendor and contractor access management, including access paths covered by business associate agreements. Participation in incident response for data-related events. Reliability Backup, restore and disaster recovery — including published RPO and RTO targets and restore tests that are actually performed, not just documented. Detection and resolution of source-to-warehouse synchronization gaps. Root-cause analysis of data inconsistencies, including cases where the source system holds several conflicting copies of the same fact. Documentation and continuity Platform documentation, runbooks, and data lineage from source through to the reporting layer. This is a first-class responsibility, not an afterthought — undocumented dependencies are our single largest operational risk today. Cross-training and written procedures, so no critical process depends on one person. Partnership Data Architect, Data Modelers, Data Developers and Analytics leadership. The EHR and application teams, and our EHR vendor's technical staff. Configuration changes are made in the application land in our warehouse, so this role is one of the few that has to see both sides. These teams currently plan separately; helping to close that gap is part of the job. Finance, on platform cost and forecasting. Education Qualifications Bachelor’s degree required in information technology, Healthcare Administration, Health Information Management, Healthcare Informatics, Computer Science, Business, or related field preferred; Associate Degree and 7 years equivalent experience may be considered in lieu of degree. Professional Qualifications Five or more years administering relational databases in production, including SQL Server or Azure SQL. Demonstrated performance tuning on large transactional datasets. Hands-on experience with Azure data services, including pipeline monitoring and failure triage. Troubleshooting synchronization between a source system and a downstream warehouse. Comfort working with source data that is poorly documented, denormalized or hierarchically structured — and the discipline to write down what you learn. Working knowledge of HIPAA safeguards as they apply to database and platform administration. Healthcare (EHR or revenue cycle) or financial systems experience preferred. Microsoft Fabric and/or Synapse preferred. Experience supporting a site or entity consolidation — merging, mapping or retiring facility-level data preferred. Infrastructure-as-code or scripted deployment, and source control for database objects preferred. Competencies Administers relational database platforms in production — backup and recovery, high availability, capacity and storage planning, patching and upgrades Diagnoses performance problems using execution plans, indexing, statistics and partitioning; establishes baselines rather than reacting to complaints Writes and tunes SQL fluently, and reads code written by others Implements database security: role-based access control, least privilege, encryption, masking, audit logging and periodic access review Safeguards protected health information in accordance with HIPAA at the database and platform layer Monitors data pipelines and integrations (APIs/web services, SFTP/file feeds, middleware), triages failures, and documents re-run and remediation steps Works effectively with poorly documented source systems — infers structure, validates findings with subject-matter experts, and records what is learned Owns platform reliability end to end, including escalation and incident response Applies change control discipline: release readiness, testing coordination, backout planning and deployment standards Treats documentation as a deliverable — runbooks, data lineage, interface and architecture diagrams, knowledge base articles Manage competing priorities with sound judgment, follow-through and appropriate escalation Explains technical constraints, configuration options, access controls and data considerations to technical and non-technical audiences Builds credibility and influences without authority across business owners, super users, clinical and operational staff, InfoSec/Compliance and leadership Manages vendor technical relationships, including holding a vendor to a commitment Transfers knowledge so that no critical procedure depends on one person A ccanto’s Commitment to Equal Opportunity: Accanto is an Equal Opportunity Employer. review_candidates.description: At Accenture Federal Services, nothing matters more than helping the US federal government make the nation stronger and safer and life better for people. Our 13,000+ people are united in a shared purpose to pursue the limitless potential of technology and ingenuity for clients across defense, national security, public safety, civilian, and military health organizations. Join Accenture Federal Services, a technology company within global Accenture. Recognized as a Glassdoor Top 100 Best Place to Work, we offer a collaborative and caring community where you feel like you belong and are empowered to grow, learn and thrive through hands-on experience, certifications, industry training and more. Join us to drive positive, lasting change that moves missions and the government forward! The work: The SharePoint & Power Platform Support Specialist serves as a frontline technical resource supporting customers across enterprise Microsoft collaboration platforms. Your role focuses on diagnosing and resolving issues related to SharePoint (2019, SE, SPO), Power Apps, Power Automate, and Power BI, while ensuring users receive timely, accurate, and customer centric assistance. The specialist leverages a solid understanding of Microsoft licensing, permissions models, and environment nuances across unclassified and classified government implementations. In addition to core support efforts, while we assist our customers in migrating from legacy products to modern cloud-based M365, this role will assist customers to troubleshoot legacy SharePoint customizations, workflows, and custom web apps before escalating to subject matter experts. The ideal candidate is proactive, highly organized, excellent with customers, and consistent in documenting work and managing tickets. Key Responsibilities: Provide Tier 1/Tier 2 support for SharePoint and Power Platform users, including issue intake, triage, troubleshooting, and resolution. Assist users in diagnosing issues related to SharePoint permissions, site architecture, content access, document management, and Power Platform functionality (Power Apps, Power Automate, Power BI). Troubleshoot functional issues in 2013 workflows, SharePoint Designer–based processes, and legacy customizations; escalate to senior engineers when advanced remediation is required. Support team, clients, and guide customers in understanding Microsoft licensing, permission structures, and governance across SharePoint 2019, SE, SPO, M365, and specialized environments. Maintain accurate, timely, and complete documentation in ticketing systems, including troubleshooting steps, resolutions, and follow up actions. Collaborate with senior engineering teams to escalate complex issues, convey customer context, and support efficient resolution cycles. Proactively identify recurring issues, propose improvements to knowledge articles, and contribute to a stable, well documented support ecosystem. Deliver exceptional customer service, ensuring users feel supported, informed, and confident throughout the troubleshooting process. Here is what you need: Minimum 3 years of hands on administration experience with SharePoint (on prem and/or cloud) and Microsoft Power Platform. Proficiency using SharePoint Administration Manager (SAM). Experience supporting end users in troubleshooting SharePoint, Power Apps, Power Automate, and Power BI. Working knowledge of Microsoft licensing models, permission structures, and access management for enterprise and government environments (SharePoint 2019, SE, SPO, M365, Copilot, Workflow Manager 2.0, SAM). Familiarity with 2013 workflows, SharePoint Designer, and legacy customizations, with the ability to troubleshoot at a functional level. Strong communication and customer engagement skills; able to translate technical concepts into user friendly guidance. Proven ability to remain organized, follow processes, and maintain consistent documentation in ticketing tools. Active Top Secret clearance required. Willingness to work on site in Washington, DC. Bonus points if you have: Experience working in environments undergoing modernization or transitions from legacy SharePoint components. Exposure to Power Platform governance, solution lifecycle management.
